questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Arabic term used to describe the state of pre-Islamic Arabian society, particularly its widespread idolatry and moral decadence, is
questions.explanation: Jahiliyyah, literally 'ignorance', denotes the pre-Islamic era in Arabia marked by idol worship, tribal feuds, and various social ills.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Before the rise of Islam, the custodianship (Sadanah) of the Ka'bah and control of Makkah's affairs was held by the tribe of
questions.explanation: The Quraysh were the dominant tribe of Makkah, and various clans within it held privileged offices connected with the Ka'bah, such as providing water and guarding the sanctuary.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among pre-Islamic Arabs, disputes between individuals or tribes were frequently settled through
options: retaliatory tribal warfare and the law of the strongest
questions.explanation: In the absence of a central authority, pre-Islamic Arab tribes often resolved disputes through raids, feuds, and retaliation, with strength and tribal solidarity determining outcomes.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The annual markets or fairs held in pre-Islamic Arabia, such as Ukaz, were mainly significant for
options: the appointment of tribal chiefs by ballot
trade and the recitation and judging of poetry
questions.explanation: Fairs like Ukaz combined commerce with cultural activity, especially poetic contests where the finest verses were publicly honoured.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pre-Islamic Arab custom in which a man could inherit his deceased father's widow (other than his own mother) as a wife is an example of a practice that Islam later
questions.explanation: Islam reformed inheritance and marriage laws, explicitly prohibiting such customs to protect women's dignity and rights.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which pre-Islamic Arabian city was especially renowned as a centre of long-distance trade linking Yemen in the south to Syria in the north?
questions.explanation: Makkah's position on the caravan route between Yemen and Syria made it a vital commercial centre, a role the Quraysh capitalised on.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In pre-Islamic Arabian belief, idols such as al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat were regarded as
options: purely artistic sculptures without religious value
intermediaries believed to bring worshippers closer to Allah
the sole and only deities, with no belief in a supreme God at all
questions.explanation: Despite worshipping idols, many pre-Islamic Arabs still acknowledged Allah as a supreme creator, but treated idols as intercessors, a practice the Qur'an condemns as shirk.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pre-Islamic Arabian institution known as 'Hilf al-Fudul', which Prophet Muhammad praised even after prophethood, was primarily a
options: treaty establishing trade monopolies for the Quraysh
pact formed to defend the oppressed and ensure justice for victims of wrongdoing
alliance for waging war against Persia
questions.explanation: Hilf al-Fudul was a chivalrous alliance among some Makkan clans pledging to support the wronged and oppressed, a value the Prophet later affirmed he would still uphold under Islam.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of these best describes the general religious landscape of Arabia just before Islam, beyond dominant idolatry?
options: The entire peninsula was uniformly Christian
Buddhism was the second most practised faith
There was no religious diversity of any kind
Small communities of Jews and Christians also existed alongside pockets of Hanif monotheists
questions.explanation: Alongside the polytheistic majority, Jewish communities (notably in Yathrib and Khaybar), some Christians (as in Najran), and Hanifs who rejected idolatry were present in pre-Islamic Arabia.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pre-Islamic practice of 'Wa'd al-Banat', condemned in the Qur'an, refers to
options: the naming ceremony of a newborn
the seclusion of women after marriage
the giving of dowry to a bride
the burying alive of infant daughters
questions.explanation: Wa'd al-Banat describes the abhorrent practice of female infanticide among some pre-Islamic Arab tribes, which the Qur'an strongly denounces.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) belonged to which clan of the Quraysh tribe?
questions.explanation: The Prophet was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh, a respected clan associated with the custodianship of the Ka'bah's water supply.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Before receiving prophethood, Muhammad (S.A.W) earned a reputation among the Makkans for his honesty, which led them to give him the title
questions.explanation: Long before revelation began, Muhammad was widely known and trusted as 'Al-Amin' for his integrity in commerce and personal dealings.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The angel who delivered the first revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad in the Cave of Hira was
questions.explanation: Angel Jibril was the messenger appointed by Allah to convey divine revelation to Prophet Muhammad throughout his mission.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The first person to accept Islam among the Prophet's household was his wife
questions.explanation: Khadijah, the Prophet's first wife, was the very first person to believe in and support his prophetic message.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among men, the first person outside the Prophet's immediate household to accept Islam was
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was among the earliest and most prominent converts, using his influence to bring several other notable Makkans into Islam.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The early Muslims who suffered severe persecution in Makkah and were advised by the Prophet to seek refuge in Abyssinia found protection under a Christian ruler known as
questions.explanation: The Negus of Abyssinia was known for his justice and granted asylum to the persecuted Muslim emigrants, refusing Quraysh demands to hand them over.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Prophet's journey to Ta'if in the tenth year of his mission was primarily undertaken to
options: seek support and protection for his message after the deaths of Khadijah and Abu Talib
questions.explanation: Following the loss of his two strongest supporters, the Prophet travelled to Ta'if hoping for support, but was instead met with rejection and hostility.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The night journey in which Prophet Muhammad was taken from Makkah to Jerusalem and then ascended through the heavens is known as
questions.explanation: The Isra was the night journey to Jerusalem, and the Mi'raj was the subsequent ascension through the heavens, during which the five daily prayers were prescribed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pledges made between the Prophet and a group of Yathrib pilgrims at Aqabah, which paved the way for the Hijrah, are known as
questions.explanation: The First and Second Pledges of Aqabah were agreements in which converts from Yathrib pledged support and protection to the Prophet, leading to the eventual migration.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: During the boycott imposed by the Quraysh on Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib, the Prophet's clan was largely confined to a
options: mountain valley/quarter known as Shi'b Abi Talib
coastal settlement near the Red Sea
questions.explanation: For about three years, the Quraysh socially and economically boycotted the Prophet's clan, confining them to the quarter of Abu Talib until the ban was lifted.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The main content of the Qur'anic revelations received during the Makkan period is generally characterised by an emphasis on
options: the organisation of a full state administration
detailed rules of inheritance and criminal punishment
Tawhid, the Day of Judgement, and moral reform
questions.explanation: Makkan revelations largely focused on establishing belief in the Oneness of Allah, the reality of resurrection and judgement, and correcting moral conduct, since legal/administrative rulings mostly came later in Madinah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the Prophet's early followers was famously tortured by his Makkan master for accepting Islam, repeating 'Ahad, Ahad' (One, One) under torment?
questions.explanation: Bilal, an Abyssinian slave, endured brutal torture for his faith yet steadfastly affirmed the Oneness of Allah, later becoming the first muezzin of Islam.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Hijrah of Prophet Muhammad from Makkah to Madinah took place in the Gregorian year
questions.explanation: The Hijrah occurred in 622 CE and was later adopted as the starting point of the Islamic (Hijri) lunar calendar.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Immediately upon arriving in Madinah, one of the first major actions Prophet Muhammad undertook was to
options: declare war on the Quraysh of Makkah
abolish all existing trade in the city
establish a mosque and formalise brotherhood (Mu'akhat) between Muhajirun and Ansar
questions.explanation: In Madinah, the Prophet built a mosque as a communal centre and paired emigrants (Muhajirun) with Madinan hosts (Ansar) in a bond of brotherhood to aid social and economic integration.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The document drawn up by Prophet Muhammad to regulate relations among Muslims, Jews, and other groups in Madinah is known as
questions.explanation: This charter established Madinah as a single political community, defining rights, duties, and mutual defence obligations among its diverse inhabitants.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The first major battle fought between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah, resulting in a decisive Muslim victory, was the Battle of
questions.explanation: Fought in 624 CE (2 AH), the Battle of Badr was the first significant military confrontation, in which a smaller Muslim force achieved a decisive victory.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: At the Battle of Uhud, a major setback for the Muslims occurred largely because
options: the Quraysh used weapons unfamiliar to the Arabs
the battle was fought without the Prophet's presence
a group of archers left their assigned post in pursuit of spoils
questions.explanation: Despite initial Muslim gains, archers stationed on a hill abandoned their post against the Prophet's instructions, allowing the Makkan cavalry to counterattack and turn the tide.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) is notable for the Muslims' defensive strategy of
options: digging a trench around exposed parts of Madinah on the suggestion of Salman al-Farisi
forming a direct alliance with the Quraysh
questions.explanation: Salman al-Farisi, a Persian companion, suggested digging a trench, an unfamiliar tactic in Arabia that successfully thwarted the confederate siege of Madinah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The 628 CE agreement between the Muslims and the Quraysh that, despite seemingly unfavourable terms, allowed Islam to spread more peacefully is known as
questions.explanation: Although its terms initially appeared to favour the Quraysh, the truce of Hudaybiyyah created a period of peace during which Islam spread rapidly across Arabia.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Makkah came under Muslim control largely without bloodshed in the year
options: 632 CE, the year of the Prophet's death
624 CE, following the Battle of Badr
630 CE, known as the Conquest (Fath) of Makkah
questions.explanation: The Conquest of Makkah in 630 CE occurred with minimal resistance, after which the Prophet granted a general amnesty to the Makkans and destroyed the idols in the Ka'bah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In his Farewell Sermon (Khutbat al-Wada), delivered near Makkah shortly before his death, Prophet Muhammad emphasised themes including
options: the annexation of Persian and Roman territories
the abolition of the Hajj pilgrimage
the establishment of a hereditary caliphate
the sanctity of life and property, equality of believers, and rights of women
questions.explanation: The Farewell Sermon summarised core Islamic ethical and social principles, including the sanctity of life, property, and honour, racial equality, and the rights of women.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) passed away in the year
questions.explanation: The Prophet died in Madinah in 632 CE, corresponding to the 11th year after the Hijrah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Muhajirun, as referred to in early Islamic history, were
options: the original inhabitants of Madinah who supported the Prophet
the Prophet's Companions who never left Makkah
Muslims who emigrated from Makkah to Madinah
questions.explanation: 'Muhajirun' (emigrants) refers to Makkan Muslims who left their homes to migrate to Madinah, distinguishing them from the Ansar, the Madinan 'helpers'.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The term 'Ansar' in early Islamic history designates
options: the Quraysh leaders who opposed the Prophet
the Madinan Muslims who welcomed and supported the emigrants from Makkah
the Prophet's bodyguards during military campaigns
questions.explanation: The Ansar ('helpers') were the native Muslims of Madinah (from the Aws and Khazraj tribes) who hosted and supported the Muhajirun after the Hijrah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Al-Khulafa Ar-Rashidun) are, in chronological order,
options: Umar, Uthman, Abu Bakr, and Ali
Ali, Umar, Abu Bakr, and Uthman
Abu Bakr, Ali, Umar, and Uthman
Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali
questions.explanation: The Rashidun Caliphs succeeded one another in this order, each contributing distinctly to the consolidation and expansion of the early Muslim state.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Immediately after the death of Prophet Muhammad, the first challenge that Caliph Abu Bakr had to address was
options: an invasion by the Byzantine Empire
the Wars of Apostasy (Ridda Wars) against tribes that renounced Islam or refused Zakat
the loss of Madinah to the Quraysh
a civil war between the Muhajirun and Ansar
questions.explanation: Following the Prophet's death, several Arab tribes apostatised or refused to pay Zakat; Abu Bakr firmly suppressed these rebellions in the Ridda Wars.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One of Caliph Abu Bakr's most significant and lasting achievements was
options: initiating the compilation of the Qur'an into a single written text
questions.explanation: Concerned by the loss of Qur'an reciters in battle, Abu Bakr commissioned Zayd ibn Thabit to collect the scattered revelations into a single authoritative manuscript.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab is particularly remembered for introducing
options: the practice of congregational Friday prayer
the compilation of Hadith into written books
the Hijri calendar and formal administrative institutions such as the Diwan
questions.explanation: Umar's caliphate saw major administrative reforms, including adopting the Hijrah as the starting point of the Islamic calendar and creating registers (Diwan) for state affairs and stipends.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Under Caliph Umar's rule, major territorial expansions brought which two empires' territories substantially under Muslim control?
questions.explanation: During Umar's reign, Muslim armies achieved major victories against both the Byzantines (in Syria and Egypt) and the Sasanian Persians (in Iraq and Persia).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Caliph Uthman ibn Affan's most significant contribution to the preservation of Islamic scripture was
options: translating the Qur'an into Persian and Greek
banning the recitation of the Qur'an in public
standardising the Qur'anic text into one official version and distributing copies to major provinces
questions.explanation: To resolve growing variations in recitation across the expanding empire, Uthman standardised the Qur'anic text (the 'Uthmanic codex') and sent authoritative copies to key regions.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The assassination of Caliph Uthman ibn Affan led directly to
options: the immediate collapse of the Islamic state
the outbreak of the first civil strife (Fitnah) within the Muslim community
a peaceful transfer of power without incident
the conversion of the Byzantine Empire to Islam
questions.explanation: Uthman's assassination created deep political divisions, sparking the first major civil conflict (Fitnah) among Muslims, notably the Battle of the Camel and the Battle of Siffin.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib's caliphate was largely dominated by internal conflict, most notably the
options: wars against the Byzantine Empire alone
Battles of the Camel and Siffin
questions.explanation: Ali's reign was marked by internal Muslim conflicts, including the Battle of the Camel against Aishah, Talhah, and Zubayr, and the Battle of Siffin against Mu'awiyah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The arbitration crisis following the Battle of Siffin, which Caliph Ali reluctantly accepted, led to the emergence of a dissenting group known as the
questions.explanation: The Khawarij broke away from Ali's camp in protest against the arbitration, considering it a violation of divine judgement, and later became a militant opposition group.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The period of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs is generally regarded by Sunni Muslims as significant chiefly because
options: they ruled for over a century as a single unbroken dynasty
these caliphs were closely guided by the Prophetic example (Sunnah) and elected/chosen through community consultation
they were all direct blood descendants of the Prophet in an unbroken hereditary line
the caliphate became strictly hereditary from Abu Bakr onward
questions.explanation: Unlike later hereditary dynasties, the Rashidun caliphs came to power through differing forms of community consultation (Shura) or nomination, and are esteemed for closely following the Prophet's example.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Islam is generally believed to have reached West Africa mainly through
options: direct military conquest by Arabian armies
trans-Saharan trade routes linking North Africa to West African kingdoms
sea routes from the Persian Gulf to the Guinea coast
questions.explanation: Muslim traders travelling the trans-Saharan trade routes gradually introduced Islam to West African societies, especially through contact with rulers and merchant communities.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the early West African empires, Islam gained significant royal patronage relatively early in
questions.explanation: The empires of ancient Ghana and, more prominently, Mali were among the earliest West African states where rulers embraced Islam and it received royal support.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Mali Emperor famed for his extravagant pilgrimage to Makkah in 1324, which spread awareness of West African wealth across the Muslim world, was
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's lavish Hajj journey, during which he famously distributed large quantities of gold, brought international attention to the wealth and Islamic character of the Mali Empire.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Songhai ruler who significantly strengthened Islamic governance, scholarship, and administration, notably supporting the scholarly centre of Timbuktu, was
questions.explanation: Askia Muhammad promoted Islamic learning and law within the Songhai Empire, and made his own pilgrimage to Makkah, further cementing Islam's role in the state.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Timbuktu, in the Songhai Empire, became especially renowned in West African Islamic history as a
options: centre of Islamic scholarship, particularly around Sankore University/Mosque
site of the first mosque built in West Africa
questions.explanation: Timbuktu, especially its Sankore institution, developed into a major hub of Islamic learning, attracting scholars and students from across the region.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Uthman Dan Fodio led his famous jihad in the early nineteenth century primarily in the region now known as
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad (beginning 1804) was waged in Hausaland, aiming to reform what he saw as corrupt and syncretic religious practice among Hausa rulers.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One of the central grievances that motivated Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad against the Hausa rulers was
options: a succession dispute within his own family
the mixing of Islamic practice with un-Islamic customs and oppressive taxation of the populace
a dispute over trade routes with Europeans
the Hausa rulers' complete rejection of Islam
questions.explanation: Dan Fodio criticised the syncretism, injustice, and heavy taxation practised by many Hausa rulers, calling for a purer application of Islamic law and governance.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic state established as a result of Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad, with its capital eventually at Sokoto, is known as the
questions.explanation: The Sokoto Caliphate emerged from Dan Fodio's jihad as a major Islamic state uniting much of Hausaland under centralised Islamic governance.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: After Uthman Dan Fodio, leadership of the Sokoto Caliphate's administration was notably carried on by his son
questions.explanation: Muhammad Bello succeeded his father as leader in Sokoto, consolidating and administering the new caliphate and founding the town of Sokoto as its capital.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The spread of Islam into the forest regions of what is now south-western Nigeria (Yorubaland) occurred mainly through
options: gradual trade contacts and later the influence of returning ex-slaves and itinerant clerics
the direct jihad campaigns of Uthman Dan Fodio himself
questions.explanation: Islam reached Yorubaland gradually, largely via trade with the north and the activities of Muslim clerics, with further growth aided later by returning liberated Muslims such as the Saro.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Kanem-Bornu Empire, located around Lake Chad, is historically significant in West African Islamic history for
options: being one of the earliest and longest-surviving Islamic states in the region
resisting all contact with Islam until colonial rule
questions.explanation: Kanem-Bornu adopted Islam very early (from around the 11th century) and persisted as an Islamic polity for many centuries, making it one of West Africa's most enduring Muslim states.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Qur'an, as a source of Islamic law and guidance, is understood by Muslims to be
options: a collection of the Prophet's personal sayings and reflections
a translated version of earlier Jewish and Christian scriptures
the literal, unaltered word of Allah revealed to Prophet Muhammad through Angel Jibril
a historical record compiled entirely by early scholars
questions.explanation: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the direct, verbatim revelation from Allah, transmitted through Angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad over approximately 23 years.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad over a period of approximately
questions.explanation: Revelation of the Qur'an occurred gradually over roughly 23 years, spanning both the Makkan and Madinan periods of the Prophet's mission.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The scribe most closely associated with recording revelation during the Prophet's lifetime and later leading the Qur'an's compilation under Abu Bakr was
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit served as one of the Prophet's principal scribes of revelation and was later entrusted with compiling the Qur'an into a single manuscript.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The chapters of the Qur'an are called
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is divided into 114 chapters known as Surahs, each further composed of verses called Ayahs.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: For the purposes of recitation and memorisation, the Qur'an is commonly divided into how many equal parts (Juz)?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is traditionally divided into 30 sections (Juz/Ajza) to facilitate its recitation across the days of a month, particularly during Ramadan.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Fatihah, recited in every unit (Rak'ah) of the five daily prayers, is notable for
options: containing the longest chapter of the Qur'an
opening the Qur'an and summarising its core themes of praise, guidance, and supplication
being revealed entirely in the Madinan period
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fatihah, 'The Opening', is a concise chapter praising Allah and asking for guidance, and its recitation is an essential part of every unit of the ritual prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is particularly notable in Islamic teaching for
options: its concise and powerful declaration of the absolute Oneness of Allah (Tawhid)
detailing the laws of marriage and divorce
narrating the story of Prophet Yusuf
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas is a short but theologically central chapter that affirms Allah's absolute Oneness, uniqueness, and self-sufficiency, rejecting any partners or equals.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Yasin is often referred to in popular Muslim tradition as
options: the first Surah revealed to the Prophet
the shortest Surah in the Qur'an
a purely legal chapter with no narrative content
questions.explanation: Surah Yasin is widely regarded in tradition as holding a central, weighty status among the Qur'an's chapters and is frequently recited for its spiritual significance.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest chapter of the Qur'an, is significant for containing, among other things, guidance on
options: a wide range of legal, social, and moral rulings, including the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
exclusively the story of the Prophet's Night Journey
questions.explanation: As the Qur'an's longest Surah, Al-Baqarah covers extensive legal and moral guidance and includes Ayat al-Kursi, one of the most revered verses in the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A Hadith, in Islamic terminology, refers to
options: a ruling issued solely by a caliph
a reported saying, action, or approval attributed to Prophet Muhammad
a verse directly revealed in the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Hadith literature records the sayings, deeds, and tacit approvals of the Prophet, forming the second major source of Islamic guidance after the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The chain of narrators through which a Hadith is transmitted back to the Prophet is called the
questions.explanation: The Isnad is the chain of transmitters cited before the text of a Hadith, used by scholars to assess the reliability and authenticity of the report.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The actual textual content of a Hadith report, as distinct from its chain of narrators, is known as the
questions.explanation: The Matn is the wording or substance of the Hadith itself, evaluated alongside the Isnad (chain of narration) in determining a Hadith's authenticity.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A Hadith classified as 'Sahih' is one that is considered by scholars to be
options: authentic, having met the strictest criteria for a sound chain and text
questions.explanation: 'Sahih' (sound/authentic) is the highest grade of Hadith authenticity, indicating an unbroken, trustworthy chain of narrators and a text free from contradiction or defect.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the six canonical Hadith collections widely regarded as most authoritative by Sunni Muslims, the two considered most rigorously authenticated are commonly known as
options: Sunan at-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah
Sunan Abu Dawud and Sunan an-Nasa'i
questions.explanation: Compiled respectively by Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim, these two collections are traditionally regarded by Sunni scholars as the most rigorously verified of the Hadith compilations.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari, compiler of one of the most authoritative Hadith collections, is especially noted for his
options: role as a Rightly Guided Caliph
compilation of the Qur'an under Caliph Uthman
extremely rigorous criteria in verifying the authenticity of each Hadith he included
reliance mainly on unverified oral traditions without scrutiny
questions.explanation: Al-Bukhari is renowned for his exceptionally strict methodology in authenticating Hadith, examining narrators' reliability and the continuity of transmission chains before inclusion.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The preservation of the Qur'an, in addition to its being written down, was also significantly reinforced during the Prophet's lifetime and after through
options: extensive oral memorisation (Hifz) by numerous companions
storage exclusively in a single royal archive
translation into multiple languages immediately after revelation
questions.explanation: Alongside written records, many companions memorised the Qur'an in its entirety, providing a strong oral safeguard that complemented the written text in ensuring its preservation.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The scholarly discipline concerned with the interpretation and explanation of Qur'anic verses is known as
questions.explanation: Tafsir refers to the field of Qur'anic exegesis, in which scholars explain the meanings, context, and implications of Qur'anic verses.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Tawhid, the foundational concept of Islamic belief, refers to
options: the collection of the Prophet's sayings
the body of Islamic civil law
the pilgrimage rites performed in Makkah
the absolute Oneness and uniqueness of Allah
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the core Islamic doctrine affirming that Allah is one, without partner, equal, or division, in His essence, attributes, and right to worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The opposite of Tawhid, namely associating partners with Allah in worship, is termed
questions.explanation: Shirk is regarded in Islam as the gravest sin, involving the ascription of divinity, power, or worship-worthiness to anything besides Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Scholars commonly divide Tawhid into three interconnected categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and
questions.explanation: The three categories are Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship), Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Worship), and Tawhid al-Asma was-Sifat (Oneness of Allah's Names and Attributes).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah specifically concerns belief in Allah's
options: role as lawgiver in matters of Fiqh
sole role as Creator, Sustainer, and Controller of the universe
questions.explanation: This category of Tawhid affirms that Allah alone creates, sustains, and governs all that exists, without partner in these functions.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The category of Tawhid concerned specifically with directing all acts of worship exclusively to Allah alone is
questions.explanation: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (also called Tawhid al-Ibadah) requires that prayer, supplication, and all forms of worship be directed to Allah alone, with no intermediary or partner.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In Islamic terminology, acts of worship performed to draw closer to Allah, such as Salah, Sawm, and Hajj, are collectively termed
questions.explanation: Ibadah refers broadly to acts of devotion and worship prescribed by Islam, encompassing ritual acts such as prayer, fasting, almsgiving, and pilgrimage.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Five Pillars of Islam are the Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and
questions.explanation: The Five Pillars form the foundational framework of Muslim practice: the declaration of faith, prayer, almsgiving, fasting, and pilgrimage to Makkah for those able.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The declaration of faith that constitutes the first Pillar of Islam is known as the
questions.explanation: The Shahadah is the testimony affirming there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger, forming the entry point into the Islamic faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Zakat, the third Pillar of Islam, is best described as
options: an obligatory charitable levy on qualifying wealth, given to specified categories of recipients
a purely voluntary act of charity with no fixed rate
a tax paid only by non-Muslims living under Muslim rule
questions.explanation: Zakat is a compulsory, calculated portion of a Muslim's qualifying wealth, distributed to specific categories of beneficiaries such as the poor and needy, distinguishing it from voluntary charity (Sadaqah).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The fasting prescribed as obligatory during the month of Ramadan is referred to as
questions.explanation: Sawm is the obligatory fast observed from dawn to sunset throughout the month of Ramadan, one of the Five Pillars of Islam.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pilgrimage to Makkah, obligatory once in a lifetime for financially and physically capable Muslims, is known as
questions.explanation: Hajj is the major pilgrimage performed during a specific period in the Islamic month of Dhul-Hijjah, and is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Unlike Hajj, the lesser pilgrimage that can be performed at any time of the year is called
questions.explanation: Umrah shares some rites with Hajj, such as Tawaf and Sa'i, but is shorter, not obligatory, and may be performed at any time outside the fixed Hajj season.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The body of Islamic jurisprudence dealing with legal rulings derived from the Qur'an, Sunnah, and other recognised sources is known as
questions.explanation: Fiqh refers to the human scholarly effort of deriving detailed legal rulings from the primary sources of Islamic law.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The independent legal reasoning exercised by qualified jurists to derive rulings on matters not explicitly addressed in the Qur'an or Sunnah is called
questions.explanation: Ijtihad is the process by which a qualified scholar (Mujtahid) applies rigorous reasoning to derive legal rulings on new or unaddressed issues.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The consensus of qualified Muslim jurists on a particular point of Islamic law is termed
questions.explanation: Ijma refers to the collective agreement of qualified scholars on a legal ruling, recognised as one of the secondary sources of Islamic law.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The method of legal reasoning that extends an existing ruling to a new, similar case based on a shared underlying cause is known as
options: Ijtihad in its general sense only
questions.explanation: Qiyas involves deriving a ruling for a new situation by drawing an analogy with an existing ruling, based on a common underlying reason ('illah).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Within Fiqh, the branch of law that governs everyday social and commercial transactions, such as contracts, trade, and marriage, is known as
questions.explanation: Mu'amalat covers the sphere of interpersonal and commercial dealings, as distinct from Ibadat, which governs acts of worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Under Islamic commercial law (Mu'amalat), the charging or paying of interest on loans, known as Riba, is
options: allowed only between Muslims and non-Muslims
questions.explanation: Riba is explicitly and firmly prohibited in Islamic law, as it is considered exploitative and contrary to principles of justice in financial dealings.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following acts is generally classified under Shariah as one of the major sins (Kaba'ir)?
questions.explanation: The consumption of intoxicants (Khamr) is explicitly prohibited in Islamic law and is classified among the major sins due to its harmful effects on the individual and society.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In Islamic family law under Shariah, a marriage contract (Nikah) requires, among other conditions, that
options: there be mutual consent of the parties, a dowry (Mahr), and witnesses
only the groom's consent is legally necessary
the marriage be conducted in complete secrecy without witnesses
no dowry of any kind be given
questions.explanation: A valid Islamic marriage contract requires the free consent of both parties, the specification of a dowry for the bride, and the presence of witnesses.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is the meaning of the term 'Sunnah' in Islamic scholarship?
options: A type of ritual prayer performed only on Fridays
The sayings, actions, and approvals attributed to Prophet Muhammad
questions.explanation: Sunnah refers to the recorded traditions of the Prophet Muhammad's words, deeds, and tacit approvals, forming a key source of Islamic guidance alongside the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is Zakat, one of the Five Pillars of Islam?
options: Obligatory almsgiving to those in need
questions.explanation: Zakat is a compulsory form of almsgiving, calculated as a portion of a Muslim's wealth, given to specified categories of people in need.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is the Islamic term for the pilgrimage to Makkah that able Muslims are obliged to perform at least once in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the annual Islamic pilgrimage to Makkah, obligatory once in a lifetime for Muslims who are physically and financially able.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is the significance of the Hijrah in Islamic history?
options: It refers to the conquest of Makkah
It refers to the first revelation of the Qur'an
It marks the death of the Prophet
It marks the migration of Prophet Muhammad from Makkah to Madinah and the start of the Islamic calendar
questions.explanation: The Hijrah (migration to Madinah in 622 CE) is a pivotal event in Islamic history and marks the beginning of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Who was the first Caliph (Khalifah) after the death of Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was chosen as the first of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs following the death of the Prophet.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What does the term 'Tawhid' refer to in Islamic theology?
options: The oneness and uniqueness of God
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the central Islamic doctrine affirming the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God (Allah).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is the significance of the Battle of Badr in early Islamic history?
options: It was the site of the first Qur'anic revelation
It was a peace treaty between Muslims and Makkans
It was the first major military victory for the early Muslim community over the Makkan forces
It marked the final defeat of the Muslims
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr (624 CE) was a decisive early victory for the Muslim community against a larger Makkan force, significant for morale and Islamic history.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: What is the meaning of 'Ummah' in Islamic thought?
questions.explanation: 'Ummah' refers to the worldwide community of Muslims, united by shared faith regardless of ethnicity or nationality.
